summary: Proceed with no companion. Stage 2 is a self-check fix that turns stage 1's unmeasured kernel into a measurable one at a single config-gated shape. Two details in the spec need sharpening before the build: the overflow threshold torch actually uses, and the extra bf16 rounding before RoPE.
justification: The diagnosis is plausible and points at overflow. Master's sequence is FusedQKNorm (bf16 out), then k / k_scale (bf16 / fp32 0-dim gives bf16), then .to(float8_e4m3fn) via c10's non-saturating conversion. At kv_scale 0.25 the divide is an exact x4, so the scale adds no double-rounding hazard beyond the kv_scale 1 case, and that case passed within one code. The one new failure class at B=32 / 0.25 is therefore almost certainly |4k| crossing the E4M3 overflow edge: torch writes NaN (0x7F|sign), while Triton's float8e4nv and the CUDA cvt both saturate to 0x7E. That also explains why the Triton splits=16 candidate failed with IDENTICAL numbers and why v (bytes 0) is clean. A second possible class is sign crossings near zero (0x00/0x80 vs 0x01/0x81), which are a large raw-byte distance but one code in value. Lever (1), printing the worst mismatches, settles which class it is, so it is the right first step. The mechanism for the speed claim is unchanged from stage 1: one cluster launch replaces FusedQKNorm, 3 casts, store_cache, prepare, FA3 23.7, combine 2.8 and norm-gate. It is still unmeasured in this layer. WEAKEST LINK: the realizable saving. The harvested sliding-fused-batched-decode-port replaced the same chain at decode_32 with a 22 us kernel and moved the shape only ~1.03x. The kill line (240.7 -> <236, -2%) is barely above the 1.5% noise floor, and the decode_32 load contributes <0.5% to the headline, so the headline will not read this. Judge on the sliding_cluster_kernel row against the summed incumbent rows (milestone 2), plus the PATH CHOSEN and selector-median lines. Two spec errors to fix in the build. (a) torch's c10 fp32->e4m3fn emits NaN only at |x| >= 480 (fp8_max = 1087<<20), not > 448; values in (448, 480) round to 0x7E. The hardware cvt (cvt.rn.satfinite.e4m3x2.f32, where satfinite is mandatory on sm_90) cannot produce NaN, so emulate it: saturating cvt, then OR in 0x7F with the sign where |x| >= 480 or x is NaN. The synthetic cases should straddle 448, 464 and 480. (b) 'Round normed k to bf16 before RoPE' should be done only if master's FusedQKNorm actually writes an intermediate there. It most likely does norm+rope in fp32 and writes bf16 once, and an extra pre-rope rounding would add mismatches. Let the lever-1 print decide. Note that master already ships the batch-1 _sliding_fused_kernel, which encodes k as fp32 -> satfinite E4M3 with no bf16 round and passes the judge. The judge's cache bound (8% rel L2 vs reference) is far looser than this self-check, and the strict self-check is a safety choice, not a rule.
confounders: sglang-pipeline-parity-router-hilo-m8: defines the incumbent chain (FusedQKNorm, cast, store_cache, FA3, FusedRMSNormGate) that the k-byte self-check is calibrated against. That is the target of the fix, not a timing confound.

small-t-launch-minimal-dense-chain-pdl: its PDL kernels sit after the o GEMM and the attention-side chain is plain stream order, so the cluster launch joins no PDL edge. The attention-side PDL attempt (dense-chain-stage2-attn-side-pdl) lost on sliding decode_32, so a small loss could come from launch ordering rather than the kernel. Read the kernel row, not only the shape.

full-decode-splitkv-restack-on-pdl: disjoint gate (window == 0), so no timing interaction. It does add a load_inline module to the 15-minute compile budget (3 modules, ~140 s, plus self-checks with more synthetic cases).

w2-marlin-atomic-add-t1-port / stack-align-par-sidestream-sliding1 / fa3-hdim128-head-pairing-batched / post-expert-norm-triton-small-t / marlin-block-m-cap-16: gated to T=1, batch-1 sliding, full layers, the post-expert stage or block_m. None touches the replaced kernels or their memory traffic at sliding decode_32.
interference: No companion is warranted. The gate selects exactly one scored shape (sliding decode_32), and no landed hypothesis touches the kernels it replaces, so an ab-revert would measure the same thing, and the other eleven shapes are in-run controls. The kernel is a single launch with its own profile row, so a control split would isolate nothing. The only ambiguity a single run can carry is a silent fallback (self-check miss or the selector keeping master), and the PATH CHOSEN line with its reason, the printed worst-mismatch classes and the selector medians resolve it from the log. If the run falls back again, the stage is still a diagnosis that pins the encode class for stage 3, as the hypothesis's Risk says. A second check would spend one of decode's 3 remaining checks for no added interpretability.
rules_flags: No rule problem in the design. FP8 cache, E4M3 query (no coarser), every window key, and config-only gates are as stage 1 had them.

Emulating torch's NaN-on-overflow in the cache is legal (it mirrors SGLang), and so is saturating. Scored shapes run kv_scale 1, no gated test exercises overflow, and kernel_fn must stay branch-free on values. Use a per-element select inside the kernel, never host-side logic.
The extra self-check cases must stay in prepare() on synthetic data, never on judge inputs. Keep every per-state buffer in the per-state dict (two-state rotation) and no child processes, as stated.
open_questions: Is the failing class overflow (master 0x7F/0xFF NaN vs new 0x7E/0xFE) or sign-crossing near zero (0x80 vs 0x01)? Define 'within one code' on the sign-magnitude ordinal (or decoded value with -0 == +0), not raw byte difference. Otherwise a ±0 crossing is falsely flagged, and fixing it is a correction, not a loosening.
Which overflow threshold does master hit in the self-check? Per c10 it should be |x| >= 480. Print it with the worst mismatches and confirm before hard-coding.
Does FusedQKNorm round to bf16 between norm and rope? If not, do not add that rounding. Only the final bf16 write (and the bf16 result of k / k_scale) are master's roundings.

Does stage 1's selector timing exist for B=32? It likely never ran because the self-check failed first. If it runs this time, make sure the L2 flush and whole-chain timing are kept, and print compile seconds per module to watch the 15-minute budget.
